consensus_summary: The consensus identifies the Sabbath primarily with divine rest: God’s creation rest, present spiritual rest in Christ, and final eschatological rest.
book_summary: The book identifies the Sabbath primarily as the complete sevenfold unit—six plus the crowning rest—expressed at the scales of week, sabbatical year, and jubilee count.
consensus_core_identification: Sabbath = sacred or salvific rest in God, fulfilled in Christ and ultimately consummated eternally.
book_core_identification: Sabbath = the whole completed seven, with the rest-day as its culminating one-seventh rather than the entirety of what the term names.
boundary_disagreement: The consensus centers the rest itself, especially the seventh day and its theological fulfillment. The book relocates the term’s center to the entire six-and-one cycle and treats rest as only its culminating component, extending the identification to seven-year and seven-times-seven structures.
material_contradiction: As primary identifications, rest and the complete sevenfold unit are different referents. The book does not deny that rest belongs to Sabbath, but it rejects treating rest as the whole thing symbolically named and replaces it with structural sevenfold completeness.
rationale: This is more than added precision around a shared category. The book reclassifies the consensus’s central referent—rest—as one component of a larger numerical-temporal whole. Although the two motifs can coexist, accepting the book’s explicit claim about what “sabbath” names requires replacing the consensus identification as the primary meaning.
strongest_objection: The book may be offering an additional numerical or lexical layer rather than denying the established theology of rest; on that reading, its identification would be NOVEL and complementary. Nevertheless, its statement that the rest-day is only one-seventh of what the word names presents the complete unit, not rest, as the controlling referent.
